title: fix(cli): the boot banner’s `🔑 Dev admin` says what that account will and will not see
body:
Closes #17081

## What an operator sees

Before, on a boot that seeds:

```
  🔑  Dev admin: admin@objectos.ai / admin123
      seeded on empty DB · dev only — do not use in production
```

After — captured from a real `pnpm dev -- --fresh -p 38771` boot of the showcase app on this branch, SGR stripped:

```
  ✓ Server is ready

  ➜  API:       http://localhost:38771/
  ➜  MCP:       http://localhost:38771/api/v1/mcp
      connect an AI client (Claude Code, Cursor, …) · skill: http://localhost:38771/api/v1/mcp/skill

  🔑  Dev admin: admin@objectos.ai / admin123
      seeded on empty DB · dev only — do not use in production
      platform admin — Setup, Studio and every record, but NO app-declared capability, so
      an app that gates navigation on requiredPermissions may show it an empty menu; grant
      it a permission set under Setup → Users, or sign in as an account your app seeds
```

Three dim continuation lines. Nothing else in the banner moved: rendering the same
options before and after produces a diff of exactly `8a9,11`, and a boot that seeds
nothing is byte-identical (asserted).

## The exit, chosen deliberately

Triage gave two, and required the implementer to pick and say which.

**Chosen: the second — keep the credential, make the banner say what this account will and
will not see, and name how to reach a scoped account.**

The first exit — "make the offered credential actually usable in an audience-gated app" —
is out of this lane on both of the boundaries set for this card, and I did not take it:

- It can only be reached by changing what the first-run seed creates (giving the dev admin
  a business position or an app permission set). Triage: 「⚠️ **If the fix means changing
  what the first-run seed creates**, that is a product-shape change ⇒ **stop and report**
  rather than deciding it in a PR.」
- And it is not implementable in principle from here. The platform does not know what an
  app's audiences are; the app does. `admin_full_access` can only ever carry *platform*
  capabilities, because an app-declared capability is the app's to define and grant. So
  "usable in an audience-gated app" is a promise the platform cannot keep for every app —
  which is exactly the card's own argument for its suggestion 1.

The card's suggestion 1 (`devHint` / `devLogins[]`) is the right long-term shape and is
**not** taken here: it needs a new key on a published schema in `packages/spec`, another
seat's lane, and a new key on a published payload is `yes` under the mechanical floor.
Suggestion 3 (an empty-navigation empty state) is `objectui`. Both stay open for whoever
owns them; nothing in this PR forecloses either. What is dispatchable in this lane is the
banner's own words, and triage's 「⛔ Silence is not an option」 binds.

## ADR-0115, read both ways

The prior ruling cuts both ways and I engaged with it rather than citing it.

**For.** ADR-0115 line 93 (the 2026-07-31 amendment) records a guard that was 「complete in
its refusal and silent in its permission」, and reproduced one level up the very defect it
existed to close, because 「the operator's only evidence of a degraded state is the env var
they may not have set themselves」. Its remedy is this card's second exit almost word for
word: brand the condition where an operator looks — `OS_ALLOW_DEGRADED_TENANCY` 「boots
degraded *and brands it everywhere an operator looks*」, `resolveAllowDriverConnectFailure`
「logged loudly at startup」.

**Against.** The same paragraph excludes the dev-admin seed from that warning set:
「`plugin-auth`'s `maybeSeedDevAdmin` is hard-gated to `NODE_ENV === 'development'` and
cannot fire on this path, and **a warning about a non-event spends the attention the real
ones need**」.

**Why this change is compatible with that exclusion, argued from the ADR's own text and not
assumed.** Read the exclusion's own reason rather than its conclusion. It rests on two
clauses, and this change satisfies both:

1. 「**cannot fire on this path**」 — the path is `OS_ALLOW_DEV_PLUGIN`, i.e. a *production*
   boot that took the escape hatch. The exclusion is a statement about that boot, where the
   seed is a **non-event**. This change prints nothing there: the lines live inside
   `if (opts.seededAdmin)`, which is populated from `authSvc.devSeedResult` and is
   `undefined` unless the seed actually ran. On the excluded path the banner is unchanged,
   byte for byte.
2. 「**a warning about a non-event spends the attention the real ones need**」 — this is an
   attention-budget rule, and it is honoured rather than overturned. The change adds no new
   line where there was none: it **finishes a line that was already printed**, in the
   banner's own register for qualifying a row (`chalk.dim` continuation lines, the same
   shape the `➜ MCP:` row and the missing-external-base notice already use). It adds no `⚠`,
   no colour, and no entry to the hazard set that paragraph is protecting. Escalating this
   to a yellow warning would spend exactly the attention ADR-0115 is budgeting; three dim
   lines under the credential do not.

The two paragraphs are about different subjects, and this is why they are compatible:
ADR-0115 was reasoning about a **production hazard** — a warning nobody should need,
because the seed cannot happen there. This card is about a **development-time expectation** —
where the seed did happen, the operator is holding the credential, and the platform is the
only party that knows what standing it just handed out. My honest reading is that ADR-0115
does not settle this against branding; it settles that the dev-admin seed earns no line on
the *production hazard* path, which is a rule this change keeps.

## The route is verified, not asserted

ADR-0115's paragraph is precisely about branding a state where the operator cannot act on
it, so a banner confidently naming a route that does not work would be the same defect
wearing the fix's clothes. `Setup → Users` was measured live on the boot above, signed in as
`admin@objectos.ai` with the printed password:

| measurement | result |
|:--|:--|
| `GET /api/v1/me/apps` as the dev admin | 3 apps — `showcase_app`, **`setup`** (`requiredPermissions: ["setup.access"]`), `account` |
| same call as `auditor.demo@example.com` (a showcase persona without `setup.access`) — **positive control** | 2 apps — `showcase_app`, `account`. `setup` is **filtered out**, so the `requiredPermissions` filter is live on this boot and not failing open |
| Setup nav served to the dev admin | `group_people_org` "People & Organization", gate `null`, children include **`Users(sys_user)`** — ungated |
| `GET /api/v1/meta/page/sys_user_detail` as the dev admin | contains `sys_user_permission_set` and the add action labelled **`Grant permission set`** |
| same page body, fabricated string `Grant fabricated permission set` — **fabricated control** | `false` |
| `GET /api/v1/auth/me/permissions` as the dev admin | 8 capabilities, all platform built-ins: `manage_users`, `manage_metadata`, `manage_platform_settings`, `manage_sharing`, `setup.access`, `setup.write`, `studio.access`, `manage_org_users`. App-declared (`showcase.*`) among them: **0** |

That last row is the banner's central claim, measured: the account really does hold every
platform capability and no app-declared one.

The persona table in the card body was measured on `objectstack-ai/ats`, which is not in this
session's repo scope. It is treated as reported evidence throughout and none of it is
re-stated here as my own measurement.

The route is also pinned in the suite, against the declarations that make it reachable
rather than re-spelled: `SETUP_APP.requiredPermissions` is a subset of
`ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES.systemPermissions`; the `Users` entry exists in
`SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS` and is ungated, as is the `group_people_org` anchor it lands in;
and `SysUserDetailPage` carries the grant surface. Renaming any of them reddens the pin
instead of leaving the banner pointing at nothing.

## What this does NOT change

- **The seed.** `maybeSeedDevAdmin`, the seed address, the password, the promotion to
  platform admin — untouched. `plugin-auth` and `packages/spec` were read-only for this card
  and neither is in the diff.
- **Any contract.** No key on any published schema, no exported symbol, no accepted spelling.
- **Any behaviour.** No branch, no condition, no data path. The only thing that moves is what
  the banner prints when it was already printing.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived **61**
families from the whole change set (all three paths, the `.changeset/*.md` included). All 61
were run on the merged head and reconciled:

```
Run reconciliation — 61 derived, 61 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 61 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 61 run,
  0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 61 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3).
```

Beyond the derived set:

- `pnpm lint` — whole repo, `eslint . --no-inline-config`, exit 0. Not narrowed, so no
  narrowing evidence is owed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit` — 195 files, 2700 tests,
  all passing. The diff spawns no process and boots no driver, so the `integration` tier is
  declared to CI rather than run locally.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` — `tsc --noEmit` plus `check:test-typecheck`,
  both clean.

Two notes on measurement, in case they are useful to the next runner:
`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` answer `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`
(exit 3) until a full `pnpm build`, and `check:type-check-debt` pins its own CI-shaped
6144 MB ceiling — passing a tighter `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096` makes its tsc
OOM and exit 3. Neither is a pass and neither is a finding; both were re-run to a real 0.

`origin/main` moved 8 commits during the run, so it was merged in and the derivation
re-run: the family list is identical before and after the merge (61, no additions, no
removals), and the 61 green runs above are all on the merged head.

## Declaration

Clause-②: no

`Contract-text:` — the published statement this card is measured against, `AGENTS.md:133`:

> `admin@objectos.ai` / `admin123`, override via `--admin-email`/`--admin-password`). The seeded admin is auto-promoted to …

The credential, its address and its promotion are documented, and nothing here removes or
renames any of them. Banner copy is not a contract surface; the delivered diff adds no key
to a published payload, exports no symbol, and accepts no spelling it refuses today.

## Acceptance notes

Out-of-scope observations, noted and not filed:

- `packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts` header records the banner writes to stderr because
  stdout may belong to the MCP stdio transport. The three new lines follow that rule
  (`console.error`), and the MCP row two lines above them makes the constraint live for any
  future author of this block. No defect — recording it because the next author of these
  lines is the one who would break it. Successor: whoever next edits `printServerReady`.
- The showcase app declares `showcase.export_data` / `showcase.restricted_ops` and gates
  actions on them, but its `App` itself declares no `requiredPermissions` — so the in-repo
  showcase cannot reproduce the empty-navigation shape the card reports downstream, and the
  reproduction above uses `setup` (which does gate) as the stand-in. Not a defect in either
  app; recorded so nobody reads the showcase's full nav as evidence against the card.
  Successor: none.
